title: Harbor Lantern: Strategy & People Summit
summary: Leadership gave a cross-functional update focused on finishing Q4, hiring targets and an org-level patch for oncall. Product highlighted performance wins on the serving runtime and the plan to ship an easier Private installer. People reviewed comp philosophy and timeframes. Meeting closed with 6 clear action items and scheduling smaller follow-ups.

Ethan Morales | Ship oncall runbook and paging matrix | due: 2026-12-13
Maya Lin | Share Q1 roadmap deck and model prioritization spreadsheet | due: 2026-12-03
Connor Reid | Finalize hiring plan for engineering and support (headcount + ramp) | due: 2026-12-10

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-29
Time: 09:00 PT (17:00 UTC)
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah; Ethan Morales; Maya Lin; Connor Reid; Jules Park; ~120 team members (zoom)

[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, um, good morning, good evening depending where you are. Welcome to what we're calling Harbor Lantern — our year-end strategy and people summit. We're going to run for about an hour and change, quick updates from product and eng, then people, then Q&A.

[00:22] Priya Shah: Quick housekeeping — recording is on, slides will be posted. If you have questions drop them in the Q&A or the slack thread.

[00:35] Ethan Morales: Thanks, Priya. I'll start with engineering. Quick top line: runtime wins — we've pushed PAW 2.3, uh typo, I mean release 2.3 of the serving engine. We're seeing median p90 token latency improvements of 12 to 18% on mixed workload shapes. There was a patch that improved KV cash — kv cash sorry — the KV cache hit path now avoids a memcpy on many heads.

[01:05] Jules Park: To add — the kernel selector is smarter around longer sequence lengths; we've got an experiment routing requests to quantized variants and there's a clear cost/perf tradeoff. For some customer workloads we can run a 4-bit variant with negligible quality delta, and that drops per-token cost by approx 30%.

[01:34] Speaker 6: (muted) can you repeat the quant bits — we couldn't hear.

[01:40] Jules Park: Sorry, yeah. 4-bit q8-ish path, targeted for non-latency-critical endpoints. We'll default that on Dedicated for certain tiers later next quarter.

[02:05] Maya Lin: Product context — our Q4 priority is twofold: (1) make Redwood Dedicated easier to adopt for mid-market accounts (that includes improved autoscale defaults and simpler pricing docs); (2) reduce friction for Private installs (VPC/on-prem). The Private work is a big focus because more regulated customers are asking for a predictable install experience.

[02:35] Maya Lin: We're also updating the model catalog UX so teams can pin model versions and compare perf profiles side-by-side — this was a frequent ask from platform customers.

[03:01] Audience chat: "Will the Private installer support our HSM integration?"

[03:05] Maya Lin: Short answer: yes, and we're standardizing KMS/HSM hooks. The guided installer will include steps for KMS binding and audit log shipping to your SIEM — it's not done, but it's on the roadmap.

[03:30] Priya Shah: On the go-to-market side — good momentum — usage up MoM in hosted API, some big mid-market pilots moved to dedicated trials. We still have churn risk in a handful of smaller accounts; CSMs are on remediation.

[03:50] Priya Shah: Financially, we're tracking toward plan for the quarter. There's more to do on unit economics but the Optimize recommendations (you know the batching/caching suggestions) are saving customers money and showing measurable retention impact.

[04:15] Connor Reid: People update. Hiring targets for Q1 2027: net new hires 36 headcount (engineering 18, product 6, sales+CS 8, security 4). We'll post the full plan. Ramp time assumptions are conservative at 3–6 months.

[04:42] Connor Reid: Comp and levels — quick preview: we're moving to a clearer leveling matrix and a targeted comp refresh for market adjustments. This isn't an across-the-board raise; it's targeted to address market mismatches and retention at critical IC levels. We'll publish the CEO note with principles, and follow with manager-level calibration sessions.

[05:09] Speaker 12: Is there a compensation pool size?

[05:14] Connor Reid: There's a pool, the exact size will be in the rollout note. Managers will have guidance on calibration next week.

[05:30] Priya Shah: On culture — we want to keep the autonomy we have while getting better at cross-team commitments. Examples: oncall rotations will get standardized SLAs; we'll measure triage MTTR and runbook coverage.

[05:55] Ethan Morales: Oncall specifics — Eng Ops has a draft runbook. We're standardizing escalation and paging so primary oncall is 6am-10pm local handover windows, and a true 24/7 primary for critical infra. The reason is to reduce alert fatigue and have clearer ownership.

[06:22] Ethan Morales: Also, a note about work distribution: we're limiting ad-hoc infra work during ship weeks; leads will get a freeze-week calendar to protect release flow.

[06:45] Audience: (chat) Can we get more support for async demos?

[06:50] Maya Lin: Yes — we're building a 'playground' template for demos that product and SEs can clone.

[07:05] Priya Shah: Ok, let's do a short segment on risks and tradeoffs — Jule? Jules?

[07:12] Jules Park: Two big risks: hardware capacity constraints into Feb (GPUs), and quality regressions from aggressive quantization on some LLMs. Mitigations: we've secured a limited additional fleet for Dedicated, and we have canary rollouts with auto-fallback to non-quant models when eval metrics dip. There's some noise in the telemetry so we're investing more in eval hooks.

[07:50] Speaker 3: Is there an update on procurement / marketplace listings?

[07:56] Priya Shah: Yes — we're live in two cloud marketplaces and exploring a third. That helps regulated customers get procurement friction down.

[08:15] Priya Shah: Quick shoutout to the infra team for cutting 25% of tail latency on streaming responses last month — folks noticed the streaming improvements in the demo.

[08:35] Audience: applause (emoji in chat)

[09:01] Priya Shah: Alright, open Q&A. Please keep questions high-level; we'll route deep technical follow-ups to the working groups.

[09:15] Anonymous attendee: Question about Dedicated pricing tiers and predictions for TCO versus Hosted.

[09:23] Ethan Morales: We're preparing a short benchmark document that compares Dedicated (reserved pools) vs Hosted incremental cost at 10K reqs/day with different seq lengths; Eng Ops will publish that next week. Note: Dedicated shines when you have sustained throughput and predictable patterns; Hosted is better for bursty/PLG.

[09:50] Anonymous attendee 2: Will private installs require a lot of infra engineering from our side?

[09:56] Maya Lin: The goal of the installer is to reduce the manual steps — we expect customers to provide the infra (VPC, subnet, KMS), but the guided flow will automate manifests, helm charts, and common operator steps. We will still have an SE-assisted path for large customers.

[10:25] Speaker 9: Any timeline for SOC2 recertification?

[10:30] Priya Shah: SOC 2 in progress, audits scheduled Q1. We'll share the compliance package to customers who need it.

[10:40] Audience crib: (murmur) 

[10:50] Connor Reid: Quick people AMA highlight — managers, please book time for calibration; folks on parental leave, we have updated re-onboarding guides. Also a reminder: end-of-year performance check-ins are coming.

[11:15] Priya Shah: OK, to wrap — three asks: (1) review the hiring plan and flag blockers, (2) managers calibrate pay suggestions with People by next week, (3) volunteers for a Private installer beta, email Eng-privacy.

[11:40] Priya Shah: Thank you all. We'll follow up with slides, the recording, and a short survey.

[11:48] Jules Park: Quick one — we're doing office hours for quantization experiments every Thursday starting next week.

[12:00] Meeting ends

Notes on transcription quality: some names were auto-captioned incorrectly (e.g., "KV cash"), and a few slide references were missed. There was intermittent audio drop for an EMEA region participant at ~01:05.
